$comment: Property catalog for the reference-case corpus. Written once and shared by every case: it supplies the per-property reference documentation, the guiding steps printed on a certification worksheet, and the dependency order those worksheets are issued in. Definitions are taken from the engine's own docstrings; formulas are only stated where they have been checked against a real published value.

gross_power.title: Gross power
gross_power.definition: Total power entering the system this snapshot — grid import plus PV production plus battery discharge. Equal to the sum of the source-adapter readings.
gross_power.formula: gross_power = Σ reading(a) for every adapter a whose reading is positive
worksheet_steps: Classify every adapter by the sign of its reading: positive is a source, negative a sink, exactly zero is idle and belongs to neither.
Sum the readings of the sources.
gross_power.note: Returns nothing at all if any grid / PV / battery sensor is unavailable — the total would otherwise silently under-count. A consumer dropping out does not affect it.

combined_production.title: PV production
combined_production.definition: Total power generated by the PV adapters. A PV string drawing standby power contributes nothing here — its draw belongs to standby.
combined_production.formula: combined_production = Σ max(reading(pv), 0) over the PV adapters
worksheet_steps: Sum the PV readings that are positive. Ignore any that are negative.

combined_grid_import.title: Grid import
combined_grid_import.definition: Power drawn from the grid. Zero whenever the grid is exporting.
worksheet_steps: Read the grid. A positive reading is the import; a negative one means zero.

combined_grid_export.title: Grid export
combined_grid_export.definition: Power fed to the grid, unsigned. Zero whenever the grid is importing.
worksheet_steps: Read the grid. A negative reading is the export, written positive; a positive one means zero.

combined_charging_power.title: Charging power
combined_charging_power.definition: The batteries' sink-side draw: each battery's unsigned charging power, summed. This is the CHG channel total.
worksheet_steps: Sum the battery readings that are negative, written positive.

combined_discharging_power.title: Discharging power
combined_discharging_power.definition: The batteries' source-side output: each battery's unsigned discharge power, summed.
worksheet_steps: Sum the battery readings that are positive.

combined_standby_power.title: Standby power
combined_standby_power.definition: Total standby power drawn by the PV adapters — a PV string consuming rather than producing. This is the STB channel total.
worksheet_steps: Sum the PV readings that are negative, written positive.

combined_consumption.title: Self-consumption
combined_consumption.definition: The CON channel: what is left of gross power once export, charging and standby are taken out. Computed as a residual rather than by summing consumers, so it captures the unmetered home base load alongside the metered loads.
combined_consumption.formula: combined_consumption = gross_power − export − charging − standby, clamped at 0
worksheet_steps: Subtract export, charging and standby from gross power.

sink_adapters_consumption_shares.title: Self-consumption share per sink
sink_adapters_consumption_shares.definition: Each metered consuming sink's share of the self-consumption channel. These need not sum to 1: the remainder is the unmetered home base load, which has no adapter to be keyed by.
worksheet_steps: List the drawing adapters that belong to the consumption channel — everything except the exporting grid, a charging battery and a PV in standby.
Divide each one's draw by the total self-consumption.
sink_adapters_consumption_shares.note: Reads off the meters alone, so it survives a snapshot where the provenance solve has nothing to say. What is left over from 1 is the home base load's share of the same channel.

home_base_load_power.title: Home base load
home_base_load_power.definition: Everything consumed with no sensor on it — gross power minus the metered draw. It has no adapter, competes for power like any other sink, and is derived rather than read.
home_base_load_power.formula: home_base_load_power = gross_power − Σ metered sink draws
worksheet_steps: Add up every metered sink's draw (the negative readings, written positive).
Subtract that from gross power.
home_base_load_power.note: OPEN QUESTION: where a sink's restriction cannot be satisfied, the engine currently leaves that undeliverable draw in this figure, so it can exceed gross minus metered draw. See captive-battery / source_in_standby.

sink_adapters_source_shares.title: Source provenance
sink_adapters_source_shares.definition: For every drawing adapter, the fraction of its power supplied by each source. Each row sums to 1, or to 0 when every source that sink is allowed happens to be idle.
worksheet_steps: List the sources and their output, and the sinks and their draw. Remember the home base load is a sink.
For each sink, note which sources it is allowed to draw from. An empty restriction means the whole mix.
Find any group of sinks whose combined draw exhausts every source it is allowed — such a group has no freedom and must be served first.
A restricted sink allowed the grid takes the grid before local generation.
Share what remains between the flexible sinks in proportion to their draw.
Express each sink's intake as fractions of its own draw.
sink_adapters_source_shares.note: Two guarantees hold in every snapshot: the watts attributed to a source across all sinks equal its reading, and a restriction is only ever broken when no allocation could have honoured every restriction at once.

home_base_load_source_shares.title: Home base load provenance
home_base_load_source_shares.definition: The home base load's own provenance row — the fraction of the unmetered draw supplied by each source.
worksheet_steps: The home load is unrestricted, so it draws from whatever the restricted sinks leave.
Express its intake as fractions of its own draw.

sink_adapters_restriction_deficit.title: Restriction deficit
sink_adapters_restriction_deficit.definition: Watts a sink was shown drawing from outside its allowed sources. Zero almost always: a non-zero figure means the meter disagrees with the configured restriction, not that the engine failed.
worksheet_steps: For each restricted sink, add up what it was attributed from sources outside its allowed set.
List only the sinks where that is not zero. An unrestricted sink can never have one.

gross_power_export_ratio.title: Export ratio
gross_power_export_ratio.definition: The fraction of gross power returned to the grid.
worksheet_steps: Divide export by gross power. If gross power is zero the answer is zero, not undefined.

gross_power_consumption_ratio.title: Self-consumption ratio
gross_power_consumption_ratio.definition: The fraction of gross power self-consumed.
worksheet_steps: Divide self-consumption by gross power.

gross_power_charging_ratio.title: Charging ratio
gross_power_charging_ratio.definition: The fraction of gross power charged into storage.
worksheet_steps: Divide charging by gross power.

gross_power_standby_ratio.title: Standby ratio
gross_power_standby_ratio.definition: The fraction of gross power lost to adapter standby draw.
worksheet_steps: Divide standby by gross power.

source_adapters_export_power.title: Exported power per source
source_adapters_export_power.definition: Watts of each source's output that left through the grid. An exporting grid is a restricted sink — only devices configured to export may feed it — so a device that may not export reads zero here however much it is producing.
worksheet_steps: The exporting grid is a sink, so its provenance row is the export mix.
Multiply each source's share of that row by the exported watts.

source_adapters_export_shares.title: Export share per source
source_adapters_export_shares.definition: Each source's share of the total exported power.
worksheet_steps: Divide each source's exported watts by the total export.

source_adapters_export_ratios.title: Export ratio per source
source_adapters_export_ratios.definition: The fraction of each source's own output that was exported to the grid.
worksheet_steps: Divide each source's export watts by that source's own reading.
source_adapters_export_ratios.note: Per source, not per channel: a string sending half its output to the house reads 0.5 here whatever the rest of the mix is doing. The four ratios of one source sum to 1.

source_adapters_consumption_power.title: Self-consumption power per source
source_adapters_consumption_power.definition: Watts of each source's output that were consumed in the house.
source_adapters_consumption_power.formula: consumption_power(s) = Σ attributed(s → k) over every sink k in the CONSUMPTION channel
worksheet_steps: Name the sinks in the CONSUMPTION channel: every consumer, plus the home base load.
Multiply each of those sinks' draw by its provenance row to get watts per source.
Add the watts up per source.
source_adapters_consumption_power.note: Routed through the provenance allocation, not apportioned by gross share — which is what makes a source's four channel figures sum back to its own reading. Every source is keyed, including the ones contributing zero.

source_adapters_consumption_shares.title: Self-consumption share per source
source_adapters_consumption_shares.definition: Each source's share of the total power consumed in the house.
worksheet_steps: Divide each source's self-consumption watts by the channel's total.

source_adapters_consumption_ratios.title: Self-consumption ratio per source
source_adapters_consumption_ratios.definition: The fraction of each source's own output that was consumed in the house.
worksheet_steps: Divide each source's self-consumption watts by that source's own reading.
source_adapters_consumption_ratios.note: Per source, not per channel: a string sending half its output to the house reads 0.5 here whatever the rest of the mix is doing. The four ratios of one source sum to 1.

source_adapters_charging_power.title: Charging power per source
source_adapters_charging_power.definition: Watts of each source's output that were charged into the batteries.
source_adapters_charging_power.formula: charging_power(s) = Σ attributed(s → k) over every sink k in the CHARGING channel
worksheet_steps: Name the sinks in the CHARGING channel: every battery that is charging.
Multiply each of those sinks' draw by its provenance row to get watts per source.
Add the watts up per source.
source_adapters_charging_power.note: Routed through the provenance allocation, not apportioned by gross share — which is what makes a source's four channel figures sum back to its own reading. Every source is keyed, including the ones contributing zero.

source_adapters_charging_shares.title: Charging share per source
source_adapters_charging_shares.definition: Each source's share of the total power charged into the batteries.
worksheet_steps: Divide each source's charging watts by the channel's total.

source_adapters_charging_ratios.title: Charging ratio per source
source_adapters_charging_ratios.definition: The fraction of each source's own output that was charged into the batteries.
worksheet_steps: Divide each source's charging watts by that source's own reading.
source_adapters_charging_ratios.note: Per source, not per channel: a string sending half its output to the house reads 0.5 here whatever the rest of the mix is doing. The four ratios of one source sum to 1.

source_adapters_standby_power.title: Standby power per source
source_adapters_standby_power.definition: Watts of each source's output that went to another device's standby draw. Standby is routed through the provenance allocation like any other sink, not attributed by gross share.
worksheet_steps: A PV string in standby is a sink with its own provenance row.
Multiply each source's share of that row by the standby watts.

source_adapters_standby_shares.title: Standby share per source
source_adapters_standby_shares.definition: Each source's share of the total power lost to device standby.
worksheet_steps: Divide each source's standby watts by the channel's total.

source_adapters_standby_ratios.title: Standby ratio per source
source_adapters_standby_ratios.definition: The fraction of each source's own output that was lost to device standby.
worksheet_steps: Divide each source's standby watts by that source's own reading.
source_adapters_standby_ratios.note: Per source, not per channel: a string sending half its output to the house reads 0.5 here whatever the rest of the mix is doing. The four ratios of one source sum to 1.

source_adapters_dynamic_coe.title: Marginal price per source
source_adapters_dynamic_coe.definition: The marginal price of what each source is delivering: the tariff for the grid, and zero for local generation, whose fuel is free.
worksheet_steps: The grid costs its tariff.
PV and batteries read zero — a discharging battery's energy was paid for when it was charged.
source_adapters_dynamic_coe.note: A battery appears here only while discharging, and the mix it charged on happened earlier, which a snapshot engine cannot see.
source_adapters_dynamic_coe.page_title: What one kWh from each source costs

source_adapters_dynamic_lcoe.title: Levelized price per source
source_adapters_dynamic_lcoe.definition: As the marginal price, but each local source carries its own levelized cost instead of zero.
worksheet_steps: The grid costs its tariff.
A PV string costs its configured LCOE; a discharging battery its flat LCOS.

source_adapters_coe_rate.title: Cost of electricity rate per source
source_adapters_coe_rate.definition: What each source's current output costs to buy, at its marginal price. Only the grid costs anything marginally — local generation's fuel is free — so every PV and battery reads zero.
worksheet_steps: For the grid: import in kW times the grid price.
For every producing PV and discharging battery: zero.
source_adapters_coe_rate.note: The marginal price of stored energy is zero on discharge because that energy was paid for when it charged. Booking it again here would count the same euro twice.

combined_coe_rate.title: Cost of electricity rate
combined_coe_rate.definition: The marginal cost of the power entering the house right now: only the grid contribution is priced, because local generation has no marginal fuel cost.
worksheet_steps: Convert the grid import to kW and multiply by the price.

combined_lcoe_rate.title: Levelized cost of electricity rate
combined_lcoe_rate.definition: As the marginal rate, but each local source additionally carries its own levelized cost — a PV string its LCOE, a discharging battery its LCOS.
combined_lcoe_rate.formula: combined_lcoe_rate = Σ (output(source) / 1000) × price(source), where the grid's price is the tariff and a local source's is its own LCOE / LCOS
worksheet_steps: For every source, take its output in kW.
Multiply by the grid tariff for the grid, or by that device's own LCOE / LCOS for local generation.
Sum them.

combined_lcoe_rate_corrected.title: Levelized cost rate, corrected
combined_lcoe_rate_corrected.definition: The levelized cost rate with each device's correction factor applied to its own price. The factor restates what a device's energy costs after its lifetime figures are edited.
combined_lcoe_rate_corrected.formula: Σ (reading(s) / 1000) × lcoe(s) × correction(s), over every source s
worksheet_steps: Multiply each source's levelized price by that device's correction factor, then price its reading at the result.
combined_lcoe_rate_corrected.note: The factor multiplies the price, never the finished number. Every device in this corpus has a factor of 1, so this equals the uncorrected rate — the two names still have to be told apart.

combined_coe.title: Cost of electricity
combined_coe.definition: What one kWh of the gross power costs on average this snapshot, marginally — the cost rate spread over the power it bought.
worksheet_steps: Divide the cost rate by the gross power in kW.
combined_coe.note: Zero gross power has no blended price; the engine reports nothing.
combined_coe.page_title: The blended price of a kilowatt-hour

combined_lcoe.title: Levelized cost of electricity
combined_lcoe.definition: The same average over the levelized cost rate.
worksheet_steps: Divide the levelized cost rate by the gross power in kW.

combined_export_cost_rate.title: Export cost rate
combined_export_cost_rate.definition: What the watts routed into the EXPORT channel cost, marginally.
combined_export_cost_rate.formula: Σ (export_power(s) / 1000) × marginal price(s), over every source s
worksheet_steps: For each of the four channels: take that channel's watts per source from its page in layer 3.
Price each source's contribution at its marginal price — the tariff for the grid, zero for local generation.
Add the four up and check the total against the gross cost rate.
combined_export_cost_rate.note: The four channel buckets are the cost ledger: every watt of gross power is bought once and lands in exactly one channel, so the four sum back to the gross cost rate. That identity is the check on this page.

combined_consumption_cost_rate.title: Self-consumption cost rate
combined_consumption_cost_rate.definition: What the watts routed into the CONSUMPTION channel cost, marginally.
combined_consumption_cost_rate.formula: Σ (consumption_power(s) / 1000) × marginal price(s), over every source s

combined_charging_cost_rate.title: Charging cost rate
combined_charging_cost_rate.definition: What the watts routed into the CHARGING channel cost, marginally.
combined_charging_cost_rate.formula: Σ (charging_power(s) / 1000) × marginal price(s), over every source s

combined_standby_cost_rate.title: Standby cost rate
combined_standby_cost_rate.definition: What the watts routed into the STANDBY channel cost, marginally.
combined_standby_cost_rate.formula: Σ (standby_power(s) / 1000) × marginal price(s), over every source s

combined_levelized_export_cost_rate.title: Levelized export cost rate
combined_levelized_export_cost_rate.definition: What the watts routed into the EXPORT channel cost once each source's own levelized price is charged for them.
combined_levelized_export_cost_rate.formula: Σ (export_power(s) / 1000) × lcoe(s), over every source s
worksheet_steps: For each of the four channels: take that channel's watts per source from its page in layer 3.
Price each source's contribution at its levelized price — the tariff for the grid, the LCOE of a string, the LCOS of a battery.
Add the four up and check the total against the levelized cost rate.
combined_levelized_export_cost_rate.note: These four sum to the levelized cost rate, the same way the marginal buckets sum to the marginal one.

combined_levelized_consumption_cost_rate.title: Levelized self-consumption cost rate
combined_levelized_consumption_cost_rate.definition: What the watts routed into the CONSUMPTION channel cost once each source's own levelized price is charged for them.
combined_levelized_consumption_cost_rate.formula: Σ (consumption_power(s) / 1000) × lcoe(s), over every source s

combined_lcoo_rate_corrected.title: Levelized charging cost rate
combined_lcoo_rate_corrected.definition: What the watts routed into the CHARGING channel cost once each source's own levelized price is charged for them. Published corrected, because that is the figure the sensor carries; with every correction factor at 1 it is the plain levelized bucket.
combined_lcoo_rate_corrected.formula: Σ (charging_power(s) / 1000) × lcoe(s), over every source s

combined_levelized_standby_cost_rate.title: Levelized standby cost rate
combined_levelized_standby_cost_rate.definition: What the watts routed into the STANDBY channel cost once each source's own levelized price is charged for them.
combined_levelized_standby_cost_rate.formula: Σ (standby_power(s) / 1000) × lcoe(s), over every source s

source_adapters_coo_rates.title: Operating cost rate per device
source_adapters_coo_rates.definition: What each PV's and battery's *own* draw cost — a battery's charging, a string's standby — priced at the mix that supplied it. A device that is not drawing reads zero rather than going absent.
source_adapters_coo_rates.formula: coo_rate(d) = Σ attributed(s → d) / 1000 × marginal price(s)
worksheet_steps: Key every PV and battery, whatever it is doing this snapshot.
For a device that is drawing, price its provenance row at the marginal prices of the sources that supplied it.
For a device that is producing, discharging or idle: zero.
source_adapters_coo_rates.note: Keyed by device rather than by sink, so the per-device sensor keeps a value whichever role its device is in.
source_adapters_coo_rates.page_title: What each device's own draw costs

source_adapters_lcoo_rates.title: Levelized operating cost rate per device
source_adapters_lcoo_rates.definition: The same draw priced at the levelized prices of its sources.
worksheet_steps: Re-price the same rows at each source's levelized price.

source_adapters_lcoo_rates_corrected.title: Levelized operating cost per device, corrected
source_adapters_lcoo_rates_corrected.definition: The levelized draw cost with each *supplying* device's correction applied.
worksheet_steps: Correct by the factor of the device that *supplied* each part of the draw, not by the drawing device's own factor.
source_adapters_lcoo_rates_corrected.note: A battery's charging cost is a blend of the source devices' prices, so the battery's own factor is not merely misplaced here — it is unrelated.

combined_device_operating_cost_rate.title: Device operating cost rate
combined_device_operating_cost_rate.definition: What running the PV and battery hardware costs in total: every device's own draw, so battery charging plus PV standby. The device view, as opposed to the charging channel alone.
combined_device_operating_cost_rate.formula: combined_device_operating_cost_rate = Σ coo_rate(d) over every PV and battery
worksheet_steps: Add up the per-device operating cost rates.
combined_device_operating_cost_rate.note: Equals the charging cost bucket whenever nothing is in standby. Overnight it inverts: charging is zero while standby is not.

combined_levelized_device_operating_cost.title: Levelized device operating cost rate
combined_levelized_device_operating_cost.definition: The same total at levelized prices.
combined_levelized_device_operating_cost.formula: Σ lcoo_rate(d) over every PV and battery
worksheet_steps: Add up the per-device levelized operating cost rates.

combined_levelized_device_operating_cost.title: Levelized device operating cost, corrected
combined_levelized_device_operating_cost.definition: The same total at the corrected levelized prices of the supplying devices.
combined_levelized_device_operating_cost.formula: Σ lcoo_rate_corrected(d) over every PV and battery
worksheet_steps: Add up the corrected per-device rates.

sink_adapters_coo_rates.title: Operating cost rate per sink
sink_adapters_coo_rates.definition: What every drawing adapter's own draw cost, priced at the mix that supplied it. Keyed by sink, so it covers consumers and the exporting grid as well as the devices.
sink_adapters_coo_rates.formula: coo_rate(k) = Σ attributed(s → k) / 1000 × marginal price(s)
worksheet_steps: Key every adapter that is drawing this snapshot.
Price each one's provenance row at the marginal prices of its sources.
sink_adapters_coo_rates.note: The home base load is not keyed here — it has no adapter. Its own draw is covered by the consumption channel.

sink_adapters_lcoo_rates.title: Levelized operating cost rate per sink
sink_adapters_lcoo_rates.definition: The same draws priced at their sources' levelized prices.
worksheet_steps: Re-price the same rows at each source's levelized price.

source_adapters_avoided_cost_rates.title: Avoided cost rate per source
source_adapters_avoided_cost_rates.definition: What each source's contribution to the consumption channel saved against importing the same energy. The grid reads zero: it is the alternative being priced against.
worksheet_steps: Take each source's watts in the consumption channel.
Price them at the grid tariff — what they would have cost imported.
The grid's own entry is zero.
source_adapters_avoided_cost_rates.note: Avoided cost is a gross quantity, not a P&L: it is what the energy would have cost, with nothing subtracted for what it did cost.

sink_adapters_avoided_cost_rates.title: Avoided cost rate per sink
sink_adapters_avoided_cost_rates.definition: The same euro seen from the other end: what each consuming load did not pay the grid, being the non-grid part of its own draw at the tariff. Only the consumption channel qualifies.
worksheet_steps: Key the drawing adapters in the consumption channel.
Take each one's draw less whatever the grid supplied it.
Price the remainder at the grid tariff.
sink_adapters_avoided_cost_rates.note: Never add the source side and the sink side together: they measure the same saved euro from opposite ends.
sink_adapters_avoided_cost_rates.page_title: Avoided cost, from the sink end

home_base_load_avoided_cost_rate.title: Home base load avoided cost rate
home_base_load_avoided_cost_rate.definition: The sink-side avoided cost of the unmetered remainder.
worksheet_steps: Take the home base load less the part of it the grid supplied.
Price the remainder at the grid tariff.

combined_avoided_cost_rate.title: Avoided cost rate
combined_avoided_cost_rate.definition: What the local generation feeding the house saved against buying the same energy from the grid.
combined_avoided_cost_rate.formula: combined_avoided_cost_rate = (locally supplied share of the CON channel / 1000) × grid price
worksheet_steps: Take the self-consumption channel — the metered loads plus the home base load.
Work out how much of it came from local generation rather than the grid.
Price those kW at the grid tariff.
combined_avoided_cost_rate.note: Published from both ends. The source side and the sink side measure the same euro, so they must never be added together.

source_adapters_export_compensation_rate.title: Export compensation rate per source
source_adapters_export_compensation_rate.definition: What each source is paid for the watts it exported, at its own configured compensation. Zero for a device that may not export — it is never attributed exported watts in the first place.
worksheet_steps: Take each source's exported watts.
Multiply by that device's own export compensation, from page 1.

combined_export_compensation_rate.title: Export compensation rate
combined_export_compensation_rate.definition: What the exported power earns, at each exporting device's own feed-in tariff. A device that may not export earns nothing.
worksheet_steps: For each source, take the watts it exported.
Multiply by that device's export compensation and sum.

adapters_saving_rates.title: Cost saving rate per device
adapters_saving_rates.definition: The P&L per PV and battery: what serving the house earned against the tariff it displaced, less what the device's own draw cost. Every device is keyed in every role, and an idle one reads zero rather than going absent.
worksheet_steps: Key every PV and battery — not the grid, and not consumers.
For a device serving the house: its consumption-channel watts times the tariff less its own marginal price.
For a device drawing: minus what that draw cost.
For an idle device: zero.
adapters_saving_rates.note: Consumers are deliberately absent: a load running on PV is the same saved euro as the string supplying it, and it is reported there and as the sink-side avoided cost — never added to both.

adapters_levelized_saving_rates.title: Levelized cost saving rate per device
adapters_levelized_saving_rates.definition: The same P&L with each device's own levelized cost charged against what it earned.
worksheet_steps: Redo the same rows with levelized prices in place of marginal ones.

adapters_levelized_saving_rates_correcte.title: Levelized cost saving per device, corrected
adapters_levelized_saving_rates_correcte.definition: The levelized saving with the correction factor applied to the price inside the bracket.
worksheet_steps: Correct the device's own price, then subtract it from the tariff — not the other way round.
adapters_levelized_saving_rates_correcte.note: Scaling the finished saving would move it the wrong way: doubling a string's lifetime cost would double its reported saving, when dearer energy can only save less.

combined_saving_rate.title: Cost saving rate
combined_saving_rate.definition: The net marginal saving: what local generation earned by displacing an import, less what was spent importing power into storage.
worksheet_steps: Credit each local source for the power it put into self-consumption, at the grid tariff.
Debit each charging battery for the grid power it took in, at the same tariff.
Add them up; the result can be negative.

combined_levelized_saving_rate.title: Levelized cost saving rate
combined_levelized_saving_rate.definition: The same total at levelized prices.
worksheet_steps: Add up the per-device levelized savings.

combined_levelized_saving_rate_corrected.title: Levelized cost saving rate, corrected
combined_levelized_saving_rate_corrected.definition: The same total at the corrected levelized prices.
worksheet_steps: Add up the corrected per-device savings.

adapters_financial_return_rates.title: Financial return rate per device
adapters_financial_return_rates.definition: A device's saving plus what it earned exporting. The saving values energy kept at home; the compensation values energy sold.
worksheet_steps: Add each device's export compensation to its saving.

adapters_levelized_financial_return_rate.title: Levelized financial return rate per device
adapters_levelized_financial_return_rate.definition: The levelized saving plus the compensation, less what producing the exported watts cost — which the marginal view has no figure for.
worksheet_steps: Start from the device's levelized saving.
Add its export compensation.
Subtract its exported watts priced at its own levelized cost.
adapters_levelized_financial_return_rate.note: Only the levelized side subtracts an export cost: marginally, local generation's fuel is free, so there is nothing to subtract.

adapters_levelized_financial_return_rate.title: Levelized financial return per device, corrected
adapters_levelized_financial_return_rate.definition: The same with each device's correction applied to its own price.
adapters_levelized_financial_return_rate.formula: as above, with lcoe(d) × correction(d) throughout
worksheet_steps: Apply the correction factor to the device's price everywhere it appears.

combined_financial_return_rate.title: Financial return rate
combined_financial_return_rate.definition: Every device's saving and export earnings, added up.
worksheet_steps: Add up the per-device financial returns.
